q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: WITH SOLD_TO_RED AS ( SELECT DISTINCT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS AS O INNER JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' ) SELECT DISTINCT SP.NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS SP WHERE NOT EXISTS( SELECT 1 FROM SOLD_TO_RED WHERE SP.SALES_ID = SOLD_TO_RED.SALES_ID )
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2_prompt_sql: WITH SOLD_TO_RED AS ( SELECT DISTINCT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS AS O INNER JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' ) SELECT DISTINCT SP.NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS SP WHERE NOT EXISTS( SELECT 1 FROM SOLD_TO_RED WHERE SP.SALES_ID = SOLD_TO_RED.SALES_ID )
explanation: Both queries aim to identify salespersons who have not sold to the 'RED' company. They achieve this by checking the absence of orders from the 'RED' company in the salesperson's order history.
